learning_objective: 🎯 Discover the greatest puzzle in Earth's history! Learn how continents drift, oceans spread, and massive tectonic plates crash into each other to build mountains.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Alfred Wegener proposed that all continents were once joined together in a single supercontinent called 'Pangaea', surrounded by a mega-ocean 'Panthalassa'. About 200 million years ago, Pangaea broke apart and the pieces drifted to their current positions.
Wegener proved his theory using the 'jigsaw puzzle' fit of South America and Africa, matching fossils across oceans, and similar rock ages on continents separated by thousands of miles of water.

Later scientists mapped the ocean floor and found 'Mid-oceanic ridges'. Magma rises from the mantle here, creating new ocean floor and pushing the old floor outwards. This proved the sea floor is spreading!

The Earth's crust isn't one solid shell. It's broken into massive slabs called Tectonic Plates that float on the semi-liquid asthenosphere. These plates can crash together (convergent), pull apart (divergent), or slide past each other (transform).

fun_activity.title: 🗺️ The World Map Puzzle
fun_activity.instructions: Print out a world map and cut out the continents with scissors. Try fitting the east coast of South America into the west coast of Africa. See how perfectly they lock together? You just proved Wegener's theory!

exam_tips: 📌 Alfred Wegener proposed the Continental Drift Theory in 1912. Memorize the names Pangaea (supercontinent) and Panthalassa (mega-ocean).
📌 Convergent boundaries destroy crust (mountains/trenches), Divergent boundaries create new crust (ridges), and Transform boundaries neither create nor destroy (faults like San Andreas).
📌 'Sea Floor Spreading' was proposed by Harry Hess. It explains the mechanism behind plate movement that Wegener couldn't.
quick_recap: ⭐ Continents are not fixed; they are constantly moving very slowly.
⭐ Fossils, rocks, and the jigsaw fit of coastlines provide evidence for continental drift.
⭐ Plate tectonics explains earthquakes, volcanoes, and mountain building at plate boundaries.
